audience_scope: K-3 multilingual classrooms — international schools, dual-language programs, bilingual European schools
doctrine_notes: Materials are theme-agnostic at the catalog layer; theme is selected at material-render time. A teaching package picks a theme once; that theme cascades to each composed material.

Generation pipeline default: client-side Fabric.js → jsPDF, paralleling the existing 29-app pipeline (per docs/lesson-plans/image-library-access-patterns.md §9). New material generators are HTML files separate from the canonical 29 §14.10 worksheet generators; they live at REFERENCE APPS/material-generators/ or a sibling directory adjudicated in Phase 3.
Each material consumes the existing /api/images endpoint + IMAGE_VOCABULARY without modification (per CLAUDE.md §10.3).

Materials are NOT graded for difficulty internally — difficulty differentiation lives in customization parameters at composition time (e.g., flashcard count: 6 cards = preschool, 10 cards = kindergarten, 16 cards = grade-1+).

Print-ready: each material must produce both A4 + Letter PDFs at sufficient resolution for classroom printing (300 DPI equivalent for image content). Phase 3 must verify source-image DPI before claiming the standard.

Color-vs-BW: every image-bearing material exposes a `colorMode` parameter (color | bw). Most school photocopiers are B&W; defaulting to color but allowing one-toggle BW route is load-bearing for real classroom use. BW mode auto-routes to the corresponding `*_bw` theme variants per §16.5.1 (do not require teachers to manually pick `animals_bw` over `animals`).

Article/gender auto-resolution: any sentence-frame or label rendering that includes grammatical articles (the/a/an in English; der/die/das in German; le/la in French; el/la in Spanish; il/la/lo in Italian; de/het in Dutch; o/a in Portuguese) MUST resolve articles automatically from IMAGE_VOCABULARY gender data — never require the operator/teacher to type articles. A platform marketed on multilingual K-3 quality cannot ship grammatically-wrong sentence strips.

Parent letter doctrine: body text constrained to ~Lexile 400 / CEFR A2-equivalent reading level. Recent-immigrant parents in international-school contexts may have low literacy in their home language; picture cues + simple sentence structure is required, not nice-to-have.

materials.name: Flashcards
materials.description: Single image + localized label per card. Used for whole-class introduction (teacher holds up a card and names it), small-group review, station rotation, and parent take-home practice. The bedrock vocabulary-acquisition material.
materials.generation_mechanism: image library + label text; one card per image; cards arranged in grid for printing

customization_parameters.description: How the asset set is sourced.
Theme to draw from (when imageSource=theme).
Explicit vocab keys (when imageSource=vocabKeyList; e.g., ['cat','dog','cow',...] for the farm-animals package).
Operator-specified image paths (when imageSource=manualSelection).
Number of cards.
Layout density. 4-up=jumbo (whole-class hold-up), 6-up=standard, 9-up=take-home/station-rotation. 16-up dropped: cards too small for any classroom use.
BW auto-routes to the corresponding `*_bw` theme variant per §16.5.1; default color but most school photocopiers are B&W.
Localized vocabulary form to display under image.
Prefix label with grammatical article (the cat / a cat / der/die/das form per locale gender). Article auto-resolved from IMAGE_VOCABULARY gender data — never typed by the operator.
Letter case for the label.

Back-of-card content. `translation-to-locale` puts the home-language word on the back (parent-takehome-friendly: parent sees Mandarin on back, target English on front). Requires duplex printing if non-blank; PDF emits print instructions.
Locale for back-of-card translation (when backOfCard=translation-to-locale). Distinct from the front-side `language`.
Paper size.
Front-side vocabulary locale (target instruction language).
Card border style for cutting guidance.
Round corners on each card. Default true: laminated sharp-corner cards cut kids during use; teachers always round.
Show dashed cut lines between cards.

k3_classroom_use_scenarios: Whole-class introduction: teacher holds up cards, names each image, class repeats chorally
Small-group review: pairs flip through deck, partner names each card
Station rotation: students sort cards by attribute, match to written words, etc.
Parent take-home: send the deck home for practice with grown-ups
Wall display: cards laminated and pinned to a 'word wall' for the unit

materials.name: Bingo board (with caller chips)
materials.description: 5×5 grid of images + corresponding caller chip strip. Used for whole-class listening + scanning game. Existing bingo app (§14.10) produces an interactive variant; this material is the printable companion designed for a teacher-called play session in the physical classroom.
materials.generation_mechanism: image library; 5×5 grid (24 unique + 1 free space); separate page for caller chips

customization_parameters.description: How the 24-image set is sourced.
Theme (if theme mode).
24 vocab keys (if vocabKeyList mode).
Number of unique boards. Real classrooms have 18-30 kids; default 24 covers most. Each board randomly arranges the same image set so all kids play together.
BW auto-routes to `*_bw` theme variants.
Cell content shape.
Caller chip content shape.
Paper size.
Vocabulary locale.

doctrine_notes: FREE space at center of 5×5 grid is convention-locked, not configurable.
Caller chips: kids mark cells with beans, dot stickers, or counters — no marker-style param needed.

Vocabulary requirement: needs 24 unique items minimum. If a package's vocab list has fewer than 24 items (e.g., farm-animals at 10 items), bingo is not the right material — use flashcards + matching mat instead, OR expand the vocabulary set first.
k3_classroom_use_scenarios: Whole-class listening game: teacher draws caller chip, names target, kids place a marker on matching cell
Vocabulary review: each call surfaces a vocab item; class repeats it after teacher names
Receptive-language assessment: teacher observes which kids identify the named target without peeking

materials.name: Picture cards (image-only, no label)
materials.description: Image-only cards with no text — for activities where the kid produces the label (vs flashcards where the label is given). Used for receptive-then-productive vocabulary work, sorting-by-attribute games, story-creation scaffolds.
materials.generation_mechanism: image library; one image per card; no label text

customization_parameters.description: How the asset set is sourced.
Theme name.
Explicit vocab keys.
Number of cards.
Layout density. 16-up dropped (cards too small for classroom use).
BW auto-routes to `*_bw` theme variants.
Paper size.
Card border style.
Round corners.
Dashed cut lines.

k3_classroom_use_scenarios: Vocabulary production: kid picks a card and names what it is in target language
Sorting / categorization games on the carpet: sort by color, by category, by size
Memory game (matching pairs)
Story-creation: kid arranges cards into a sequence and tells the story
Show-and-name station rotation

materials.name: Matching mat (image ↔ word pairs)
materials.description: Single-page mat with N images on the left, N corresponding written words on the right (in target language); kid draws lines or places counters to match. Teacher prints + provides; kid completes with pencil or with manipulatives.
materials.generation_mechanism: image library + IMAGE_VOCABULARY labels; left column images, right column shuffled words

customization_parameters.description: Number of pairs. K-3 default 6 — kids can lose place tracking 8+ pairs without scaffolding.
Right column: full word, beginning letter only, or another image (for image-image matching).
BW auto-routes to `*_bw` theme variants.

doctrine_notes: Differentiation from existing matching app PDF: this material targets carpet/table-mat use (full-page mat, larger cells, paired-stations mode). The existing matching app PDF is for individual-table worksheet use. Phase 3 must verify the visual/layout differentiation; if redundant after build, surface the existing app PDF as the package's matching artifact instead and cut this material.
k3_classroom_use_scenarios: Independent or paired worksheet at table
Receptive-to-print bridging (kid hears word, finds matching image, then matches to printed word)
Differentiated instruction (some kids match image-letter, others image-word, others image-image)

materials.name: Sentence strips (sentence frames with images)
materials.description: Long horizontal cards with a single sentence frame and an embedded image slot. The sentence frame is the target language pattern; the image fills in the noun. For oral-language modeling and as a printed reference during student practice. Example for vocabulary-acquisition: 'I see a [image of cat]' / 'Ich sehe eine [Bild von Katze]'.
materials.generation_mechanism: text + image library; horizontal strip layout; one sentence per strip

customization_parameters.description: Preset frames: i-see-a → 'I see a {item}'; i-have-a → 'I have a {item}'; this-is-a → 'This is a {item}'; i-like-plural → 'I like {item:plural}'; there-are-count-plural → 'There are {count} {item:plural}'; the-item-is-color → 'The {item} is {color}'; the-item-says → 'The {item} says ___' (animal sounds). Custom → use frameTemplate field.
Custom template (active when framePreset=custom). Use {item}, {item:plural}, {count}, {color} placeholders. Articles auto-resolved from IMAGE_VOCABULARY gender data — never typed by the operator.
Number of strips.
BW auto-routes to `*_bw` theme variants.
Add a blank line below each strip for the kid to copy or trace the sentence.
Landscape recommended for sentence strips.

doctrine_notes: CRITICAL: article/gender auto-resolution from IMAGE_VOCABULARY is required. A platform marketed on multilingual K-3 quality cannot ship 'Ich sehe ein Katze' instead of 'Ich sehe eine Katze'. This is the single highest QC risk in the catalog and Phase 3 MUST get this right at first ship.
Plural morphology: Finnish, Swedish, German plurals are not '+s'. The IMAGE_VOCABULARY plural data ([1] of the locale tuple) handles this; verify generators read the plural form, not noun+'s'.

Frame complexity vs age range: Pre-K/K → 'I see a {item}'; K/Grade 1 → 'I have {count} {item:plural}'; Grade 1+ → 'The {item} is {color}'. Phase 4 package authoring should match frame complexity to package age-range.
k3_classroom_use_scenarios: Pocket-chart display: teacher pins strips during oral-language modeling
Choral repetition warmup: class repeats each strip aloud
Sentence-frame scaffold during pair work: kid uses strip as a reference while practicing aloud
Take-home practice card

materials.name: Answer key (per-package)
materials.description: Single PDF summarizing the package's expected outcomes for every composed exercise + every material. NOT for students. Used by the teacher to confirm correctness during whole-class debrief or one-on-one checking.
materials.generation_mechanism: auto-generated from package definition; renders one section per composed exercise + one section per material requiring teacher reference

customization_parameters.description: Include each composed exercise's answer key.

Include reference for each material (e.g., bingo image set with names; flashcard label list). This is the load-bearing value for non-native-speaker teachers — confirms vocabulary forms in the target language.
Append the package's pedagogical-target description and assessment criteria. Default true — teachers using this platform are likely subbing into multilingual contexts they're new to.

k3_classroom_use_scenarios: Pre-lesson teacher review: teacher reads through to internalize expected outcomes
During-lesson reference: teacher consults during pair work or station rotation
Post-lesson debrief: teacher uses to model correct answers in whole-class share-out

materials.name: Parent take-home letter (with picture cues)
materials.description: One-page letter to parents in the home language of the family, explaining what the kid is working on and how parents can support at home. Picture cues embedded so K-3 kids can show parents what the picture means even if the parent's literacy in the target language is low. Distinct from the deferred ParentNote AI-feature in CLAUDE.md §7 (which is per-topic-and-language, generated by Mac Studio AI); this material is per-package and operator-authored.
materials.generation_mechanism: text + image library + sentence-frame template; one paragraph + N picture cues per package

customization_parameters.description: Home language for the letter BODY text. The parent reads this. Distinct from `language` (target instruction language).
Target instruction language — used to label the picture cues so parents see the words their kid is learning.
BW auto-routes to `*_bw` theme variants for picture cues.
Leave a blank line at the bottom for teacher signature.

doctrine_notes: Body text constrained to ~Lexile 400 / CEFR A2-equivalent reading level. Recent-immigrant parents may have low literacy; short sentences + common words + no idioms.
Picture cues are labeled with the target word, body text is in the home language. This is the bridge: parent sees the kid's vocabulary even if their target-language literacy is zero.
k3_classroom_use_scenarios: Sent home in the kid's bag at the end of the unit
Multilingual classroom support: parents who don't speak the instruction language can still understand via picture cues
Family literacy bridge: parents practice the target vocabulary at home with the kid

materials.name: Manipulative cut-outs
materials.description: 2D printable themed counters that kids cut out and use for counting, sorting, sequencing, and pattern building. Bridges the abstract (worksheet) and concrete (manipulative) for K-3 kids whose math reasoning is still hands-on. Added at Phase 1 surface gate per classroom-teacher-agent recommendation.
materials.generation_mechanism: image library; one image repeated N times on a single sheet, scaled to ~1.5in tall for finger-friendly cutting; cut guides between each item

customization_parameters.description: When non-null, generates one cut-out per listed vocab key (variety mode). When null, repeats single image N times (count mode).
single-repeat: one image x itemCount copies (counting/quantity work). variety: one image per vocabKey x N copies each (sorting/categorization work).
Total cut-outs on the sheet (single-repeat) OR copies per vocab key (variety).
Cut-out tall dimension. medium = K-3 finger-friendly cutting.
BW auto-routes to *_bw theme variants.
Dashed cut lines around each item.
Locale for any optional labels (most cut-outs are unlabeled).

k3_classroom_use_scenarios: Counting work: 'count out 7 farm animals' — concrete-manipulative bridge to numeral
Sorting / categorization on the carpet: kids physically group cut-outs by attribute
Pattern building: arrange cut-outs into AB / AAB / ABC sequences
Take-home math practice: send 20 farm animals home; parent sets up counting tasks
Story-creation prop: kids arrange cut-outs into scenes and narrate
doctrine_notes: Single-repeat mode is the most common K-3 use (10-20 of one image for counting). Variety mode supports sorting/categorization tasks where multiple item types matter.
Cut size load-bearing: too small (<1in) = K kids can't cut; too large (>2.5in) = wastes paper. Default 1.5in covers most use cases.
Phase 4 farm-animals package would compose this material in variety mode with vocabKeys=[cow, sheep, pig, ...] x 2 copies each = 20 cut-outs.
